sentiment.rationale: The document reports a significant GAAP loss per share of ($7.14) and a core loss per share of ($7.47), primarily driven by a $4.9 billion charge on the 777X program due to a certification delay pushing first delivery to 2027. While revenue improved and free cash flow turned positive, the forward guidance for free cash flow is approximately ($2.5B) for the full year, indicating continued cash burn. The structural risk of the 777X delay and ongoing production stabilization efforts outweigh the positive operational momentum, leading to a negative sentiment score.

summary.revenue: $23.3 billion, up 30% from $17.8 billion in Q3 2024, primarily reflecting 160 commercial deliveries.
summary.eps: GAAP diluted loss per share of ($7.14), compared to ($9.97) in Q3 2024; core loss per share (non-GAAP) of ($7.47), compared to ($10.44) in Q3 2024. The improvement is primarily due to higher delivery volume, but the quarter included a $4.9 billion charge on the 777X program.
summary.guidance: Free cash flow (non-GAAP) estimate for 2025 is approximately ($2.5B). The company jointly agreed with the FAA in October to increase 737 production to 42 per month. 777X first delivery now anticipated in 2027.
summary.margin: GAAP operating margin of (20.5)% compared to (32.3)% in Q3 2024. Core operating margin (non-GAAP) of (21.7)% compared to (33.6)% in Q3 2024.
key_risks: 777X program charge of $4.9 billion due to updated certification timeline, with first delivery now anticipated in 2027.
Ongoing production stabilization efforts for 737 and 787 programs.
Structural risks related to production quality, certification, and regulatory changes.
Dependence on suppliers, labor availability, and potential work stoppages.
Pending acquisition of Spirit AeroSystems and associated risks.
